verdict: No mismatch with the existing public per-frame/per-message contract. M8-007-PROTOCOL-002 is accurately restated as a bounded eager-allocation/slow-peer tradeoff; the current evidence does not establish uncontrolled allocation or a memory leak.

contract_evidence.finding: WebSocketLimits defaults maximumFrameBytes to 1 MiB, caps it at 1 GiB, requires maximumMessageBytes >= maximumFrameBytes, and caps message bytes at 1 GiB.

readWireFrame decodes the declared length, rejects length > maximumFrameBytes, validates control-frame length, then allocates exactly Array<Byte>(length). The payload allocation cannot exceed the admitted frame cap.

The aggregate fragmented-message check occurs after readWireFrame returns. A continuation may therefore allocate/read a complete frame up to maximumFrameBytes even when it exceeds the message's remaining allowance; it is then rejected with MessageTooLarge/1009. Since maximumMessageBytes >= maximumFrameBytes and the connection retains only an Int64 byte count, fragment opcode, and UTF-8 validator—not prior payload arrays—one internal payload allocation never exceeds either absolute cap.

A successful receive transfers the sole wire payload array into WebSocketFrame without cloning; caller access through payload makes a documented defensive copy. The connection itself does not retain successful frame payloads.
Generated API documentation describes maximumFrameBytes as maximum payload bytes retained or sent for one frame and maximumMessageBytes as combined data payload across a fragmented message.

Generated API documentation promises bounded uncompressed framing and says receive retains only the bounded payload; it does not promise incremental allocation, aggregate process memory admission, or immediate heap reclamation.

cleanup_evidence.logical_ownership: On cancellation, deadline, EOF, transport failure, invalid progress, invalid UTF-8, or message-limit failure, the payload/frame remains local to receive/readWireFrame. No connection field receives it. The catch path aborts or protocol-closes the transport, finally releases the reader gate, and rethrows; after receive unwinds the array is unreachable and GC-eligible.
cleanup_evidence.timing_limit: There is no explicit free and no public promise of prompt physical heap/RSS reclamation. A protocol-error path can retain the local frame while terminateProtocol performs a close bounded by closeTimeout (default 5 seconds); transport/cancellation failures abort and unwind directly. A peer that advertises an admitted length and then stalls under the default background context can keep the cap-sized allocation live indefinitely until cancellation, deadline, peer failure, or external close wakes the read.
cleanup_evidence.classification: This proves ownership release, not deterministic physical deallocation. The original recommendation's demand to prove prompt memory release is stronger than the present public contract.

bounded_concurrency.server: HttpServerBuilder defaults connectionLimit to 1024; Http1ServerConfig permits 1..65536 and admission waits while active.size reaches the configured limit.
bounded_concurrency.http2: The server defaults http2StreamLimit to 100 per connection and advertises/enforces that bound. These make concurrency finite but do not constitute an aggregate byte budget.
bounded_concurrency.implication: Worst-case concurrent pressure can still be large when operators choose high frame/connection/stream limits. That is the documented operational tradeoff; no future M10 aggregate-budget API is required or proposed here.

test_evidence.covered: One-byte transport reads, ownership/defensive copies, frame/message progression, fail-closed protocol handling, declared 64-bit length above a 128-byte custom frame cap, and a fragmented 100+40-byte message exceeding a 128-byte custom message cap.
test_evidence.not_covered: No active receive-cancellation test observes a partially filled payload, and no test can establish GC timing or RSS return. The source ownership proof is therefore the precise evidence for cleanup; no high-memory or OOM experiment was run.

source_probe.command: A read-only source-order assertion checked length-read < frame-cap-check < payload-allocation and message-check after frame read.

recommended_finding_text: WebSocket receive eagerly reserves the already-admitted frame payload size after validating maximumFrameBytes. A stalled peer can keep up to that configured per-receive cap live for the operation's duration; fragmented-message overflow is detected only after the complete continuation frame is read, so the remaining message allowance does not reduce that allocation. Cancellation/error removes all connection-owned references when receive unwinds, but Cangjie GC does not provide a prompt physical-release guarantee. This is a documented bounded-memory/latency tradeoff, not evidence that an allocation exceeds the public frame/message caps or leaks after terminal cleanup.
